title: Is Verizon an Undervalued Dividend Stock to Buy Right Now in November? | VZ Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc revisits Verizon (VZ) as SpaceX competition intensifies in telecom. Wall Street has cut Verizon's expected earnings-per-share growth from over 10% to about 7% over the next several years, which he considers realistic for a mature industry where four players now fight over existing customers. Verizon has improved its operating margin from roughly 20% in 2017 to 23.9% over the trailing twelve months, with AI helping cut customer-support costs. The balance sheet remains heavy: over $184B in debt, at or above the market capitalisation. The forward P/E of 8.7 sits mid-range in its 7-10 band of recent years, which he calls reasonable for the growth on offer. He trims his DCF free-cash-flow estimates by only about $300m a year against $23B+ of annual free cash flow, and calculates a fair value over $57 per share versus $46 current — roughly 24% undervalued. Verizon has beaten the S&P 500 year to date, up over 13% plus dividends. Call: VZ BUY (reiterated), with conviction downgraded from medium to low given the new competitive risk.

calls.price_at_call: DCF fair value over $57 vs $46 current (~24% undervalued); forward PE 8.7
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated, conviction downgraded medium -> low. Ranked a buying opportunity all year and has beaten the S&P 500 YTD (+13% plus dividends), but less optimistic now: EPS growth expectations cut from 10%+ to ~7%, FCF estimates trimmed ~$300m/yr, $184B debt at/above market cap.
calls.base_case: Low-single-digit revenue growth, mid-to-high-single-digit EPS growth; valuation stays mid-range.
calls.bull_case: AI customer-service savings lift margins (already 20% -> 23.9% over a decade).
calls.bear_case: SpaceX competition disrupts the three-carrier status quo; debt limits the 6G build-out.
